newsitem.title: USA: Micron comfortable with Q1 estimate.
newsitem.headline: Micron comfortable with Q1 estimate.

text.p: Micron Electronics Inc Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Joseph Daltoso said the company remains comfortable with analyst estimates for its first quarter to end-November, but it could have done better.

"We're very comfortable with where the Street is right now," he said of Wall Street's consensus estimate, which he said was for earnings per share of 21 cents for the quarter ended last month. The results are due to be reported Monday.

But Daltoso said after a presentation to a Montgomery Securities investor conference here that the company is disappointed it did not do much better than that. "We could have done substantially better," he added.

Micron executives said the company had an aggressive, dual processor Pentium Pro offering, but that despite a favorable allocation of Pentium Pro microprocessors from Intel Corp it had sold out of these quickly and could not obtain more of the chips, hurting the quarterly results.
"We had a great allocation," he said of the top-end Intel chips. "It probably would have been better if we'd shipped a single processor machine."

Daltoso said Intel has told it that the chipmaker should be able to meet demand for the top-end Pentium Pro machine by around the first of the year, but the company remained conservative about financial planning.
The company also noted it has some $115 million in cash.
